summary: Turns EssayCards' essay overview into a section-level learning progression (guided oral -> flashcards -> unguided oral -> essay mastery) with flashcard unlocking, pass/fail oral grading, mastery decay and revalidation.

classification.why_application: What counts as 'guided oral passed', which cards are locked, what Established/Learned mean for a section or essay, and when mastery decays are EssayCards-specific interpretations of its own essay/section/flashcard/oral-exam vocabulary (03_Application/EssayCards/CLAUDE.md glossary). Nothing here generalizes to another Atlas application.
non_goals: Removing the category-level flashcard statistics (progress_total / progress_established / the 'N / M established . K open' topic line) - kept per draft section 2
Removing essays.status or the planned/complete ingest vocabulary from the data model - only the overview PILL is removed; oral-exam buttons remain gated on status === 'complete' exactly as before
A configuration UI or env var for the 70% pass threshold or the 30-day Learned threshold - both are single backend constants this sprint (draft: 'configurable later')
Per-flashcard manual lock/unlock controls - locking is derived from section state only
Any change to FSRS parameters, grading vocabulary (again/hard/good/easy), review_events semantics or the due-queue ORDER BY (only eligibility filters are added)
Any change to review-stats endpoints (review_events is not written by a 'preserved' revalidation check, so they are unaffected by construction)
Automated in-app oral examination: scores still arrive via the existing ChatGPT export -> paste -> import round trip
Re-invalidating guided state: Section Yellow, Essay Yellow and guided oral history are never revoked by any rule in this sprint
Staleness handling when a section is edited after its oral pass (existing section_version_at is stored but not acted on)
classification.not_platform: Pass/fail meaning of an oral score, section/essay mastery ladders, card unlocking and the revalidation protocol are domain rules of this one app. The Dataset contract (platform_contracts) and platform-ui are consumed unchanged; no reusable capability is introduced.

consumes: essaycards.flashcard_review_state (review_interval is the write-time cache of next_due_at - last_reviewed_at; sole basis of Established / Learned)
essaycards.fsrs_card_state, backend.scheduling.FSRSScheduler - consumed unchanged by the failed-revalidation path
Postgres now() - sole time authority for every server-evaluated condition (R-CON-AL-06)
provides: GET /api/essaycards/essays and GET /api/essaycards/essays/{id} - CHANGED (breaking, sole consumer reworked in-sprint): the nine Sprint12 learning-progress fields and learning_level are REMOVED; replaced by essay_state and its supporting fields
GET /api/essaycards/progress/sections - NEW flat Dataset: one traffic-light row per section
GET /api/essaycards/essays/{essay_id}/examination-package - CHANGED: scope + section_id params, scoring echo
POST /api/essaycards/examinations/import - CHANGED: per-result scope, pass/fail verdict, state transitions, cascade
GET /api/essaycards/essays/{essay_id}/examinations - NEW Dataset of full-essay oral attempts
GET /api/essaycards/flashcards/due and /flashcards/stats - CHANGED eligibility: locked cards excluded (due also excludes needs_revalidation cards)
GET /api/essaycards/flashcards/revalidation - NEW Dataset (same row shape as /due): the Revalidation queue
POST /api/essaycards/flashcards/{id}/review - CHANGED: server-derived revalidation branch, additive revalidation_outcome response field, locked-card rejection
GET /api/essaycards/essays/{essay_id}/questions - CHANGED additive: is_locked, card_state, needs_revalidation per row
invariants: PASS RULE (single definition, backend/oral_state.py): score_percent = score / SCORE_MAX * 100 with SCORE_MAX = 6; passed iff score_percent >= PASS_THRESHOLD_PERCENT (70). On the existing 0-6 integer scale this is passed iff score >= 5 (4 = 66.7% fails). The same rule applies to all four oral kinds (guided/unguided x section/essay). The verdict is computed once at import time and stored in passed; nothing re-derives it later. This SUPERSEDES Sprint12's score >= 3 PASS_SCORE_THRESHOLD, which is deleted.

SECTION STATE (derived at query time, never stored; highest satisfied wins): blue iff section_oral_state.unguided_passed; else green iff guided_passed AND the section has >= 1 card AND every card has last_reviewed_at not null AND review_interval >= 24 hours; else yellow iff guided_passed; else grey. Because blue needs only the unguided pass, a section whose unguided pass is later invalidated falls back to green/yellow/grey from the SAME underlying evidence - no stored color to repair.

ESSAY STATE (derived, highest satisfied wins): violet iff essay_oral_state.unguided_passed; else blue iff the essay has >= 1 section AND every section has unguided_passed; else green iff the essay has >= 1 card AND every card has review_interval >= 30 days; else yellow iff essay_oral_state.guided_passed; else grey. Section guided orals never contribute to essay yellow. A zero-card or zero-section essay is never vacuously green/blue.

ESTABLISHED / LEARNED: established = review_interval >= 24 hours (unchanged); learned = review_interval >= 30 days (new). Learned is a SUBSET of established. Both thresholds are defined once in backend/progress.py and used by every query (card_state, section green, essay green, progress_established). Card display state is the highest of locked / new / learning / established / learned ('locked' only while the card's section is not guided_passed).

UNLOCK (derived, no stored per-card lock): a card is eligible for any review queue only if its section's section_oral_state row exists with guided_passed = true. Cards remain stored, remain counted in progress_total, and are visibly 'locked' in the question overview. A card ingested later into an already guided-passed section is unlocked automatically.
GUIDED PASS IS STICKY: a failing guided attempt (section or essay) is stored in history and updates guided_latest_score but never clears guided_passed or relocks cards.

UNGUIDED PASS SEMANTICS: a passing unguided section attempt sets that section's unguided_passed; a failing unguided SECTION attempt only records history (it does NOT clear unguided_passed). A passing unguided ESSAY attempt sets essay unguided_passed (Violet) and the date; a failing unguided ESSAY attempt made while essay unguided_passed was true triggers the FAILURE CASCADE below; a failing unguided essay attempt made while it was NOT true only records history (no cascade, no revalidation).

FAILURE CASCADE (one transaction, same one as the attempt INSERT; backend/oral_state.py): (1) essay_oral_state.unguided_passed = false, unguided_invalidated_at = now(); (2) every section_oral_state row of that essay with unguided_passed = true -> unguided_passed = false, unguided_invalidated_at = now(); (3) revalidation flagging: every flashcard of that essay whose flashcard_review_state.last_reviewed_at IS NOT NULL gets needs_revalidation = true. NOT touched: guided_* columns, section_examinations/essay_examinations rows, fsrs_card_state, next_due_at, review_interval, last_reviewed_at, review_events. Never-reviewed cards are not flagged (there is nothing to revalidate).

REVALIDATION CARD HANDLING (server-derived in POST /flashcards/{id}/review; the client sends no mode field): if the card's needs_revalidation is true, the request is a revalidation check. Grade 'again' = incorrect, any other grade = correct (single constant REVALIDATION_FAIL_GRADES in backend/revalidation.py). CORRECT: flag cleared, a revalidation_events row (outcome 'preserved') inserted, and NOTHING else changes - no FSRS call, no review_events row, flashcard_review_state timestamps/interval and fsrs_card_state byte-identical. INCORRECT: flag cleared, the normal FSRS review path runs exactly as for any card (state, review_interval, next_due_at, fsrs_card_state, review_events written), plus a revalidation_events row (outcome 'failed'). All of it in one transaction.

REVALIDATION QUEUE VS NORMAL QUEUE: cards with needs_revalidation = true are excluded from GET /flashcards/due (focus and review alike) and served only by GET /flashcards/revalidation regardless of next_due_at. This is an explicit exception to the draft's 'normal review scheduling unchanged' acceptance line: a flagged card is not part of normal scheduling until its check is done; FSRS due dates are never overwritten. Revalidation is complete for an essay when its pending count (flagged cards) reaches 0.

LOCKED-CARD WRITE GUARD: POST /flashcards/{id}/review on a card whose section is not guided_passed is rejected VALIDATION_ERROR with no write (defends against stale clients; a locked card cannot appear in /due or /revalidation).

TIME AUTHORITY (R-CON-AL-06): *_passed_at = the attempt's examined_at (external time supplied by the examiner reply, ISO-8601 with explicit UTC offset required - existing _parse_timestamp discipline); unguided_invalidated_at and revalidation_events.checked_at = server now(). State transitions apply in SERVER IMPORT ORDER (array order within a batch), not examined_at order: an older-dated result imported later is applied as if it were the newest. Unlock/lock and all colors are evaluated at query time against stored state and review_interval - no client time input exists anywhere in this sprint.

ORAL ATTEMPT IMPORT IS ALL-OR-NOTHING: validate everything, resolve every slug, then insert + apply state for each result in array order inside one transaction; any failure rolls back every attempt, state change, cascade and flag.

EXPLICIT NULL VS OMIT (R-CON-AL-04/05): this sprint adds NO PATCH or partial-update endpoint, and no user-editable field with a clear-to-null round trip. The only optional/nullable inputs it touches are on the append-only import: feedback (omitted == null == stored SQL null; unchanged), nugget_versions (omitted == null; unchanged; section scope only), and the NEW section_anchor_slug (required non-empty string for scope 'section'; for scope 'essay' it must be omitted or null - a non-null value is VALIDATION_ERROR; omitted and null are equivalent). There is no 'update an existing attempt' path, so no persisted-state clearing semantics are needed. needs_revalidation and all oral-state columns are written only by server logic, never from a client payload.

SCOPE-MODE CLOSURE (R-CON-AL-02): examination-package accepts exactly {exam_type, scope=essay} and {exam_type, scope=section, section_id}; any other combination is VALIDATION_ERROR. /flashcards/revalidation accepts exactly {} and {essay_id}. /progress/sections accepts exactly {} and {essay_id}. Every allowed combination yields a constructible, possibly empty, Dataset.

CATEGORY STATS: progress_total and progress_established keep their definitions (every card / review_interval >= 24h) and are unchanged. open_count (next_due_at <= now()) is the one category figure that must change: it now ALSO requires the card to be unlocked and not needs_revalidation, because its documented meaning is 'what a focus session would surface' (see open_questions).

All read endpoints return Dataset | ApiError (R-CON-BP-04). POST import and POST review are mutation endpoints (exempt): typed JSON record on success, ApiError on failure. GET examination-package stays the existing bespoke-JSON R-CON-BP-04 exemption (clipboard artifact for an external LLM).
failure_modes: VALIDATION_ERROR - examination-package missing/invalid exam_type or scope, scope=section without section_id, scope=essay with section_id (400)
NOT_FOUND - examination-package unknown essay_id, or section_id that does not belong to that essay (404)

VALIDATION_ERROR - import result missing/invalid scope; scope=section without section_anchor_slug; scope=essay with a non-null section_anchor_slug; plus every pre-existing structural rule (score 0-6 integer, exam_type, timestamps with offset) (400, whole batch rejected)
NOT_FOUND - import essay_slug / section_anchor_slug pair does not resolve (404, whole batch rejected, nothing written)
VALIDATION_ERROR - POST review on a card in a locked section (400)
NOT_FOUND - POST review unknown flashcard (404, unchanged)

Stale revalidation session (documented, not an error): a card cleared in another tab is simply absent from the next /revalidation refetch; a card flagged mid-session by a cascade is handled as a revalidation on its next grade

Re-import of an identical examiner reply double-applies (new attempt rows; a duplicate failing Violet unguided result cascades once, the second is history-only because the claim is already false) - accepted, same append-only discipline as Sprint12

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/essaycards/progress/sections
exposed_surfaces.purpose: One derived traffic-light row per section, in essay display order then section order, feeding the overview's small dots and the reader's section markers.

query_behavior.defaults: no essay_id -> every section of every essay
query_behavior.ordering: essays.category asc nulls last, essays.sort_index asc, essays.created_at asc, essay_sections.order_index asc (same essay order as GET /essays)
query_behavior.grouping: none - flat rows; client groups by essay_id (same idiom as /essays/{id}/questions)
query_behavior.time_basis: Postgres now() evaluated at query time; the state itself depends only on stored oral state and review_interval, not on the clock
query_behavior.boundary_construction: state rules in contracts.invariants SECTION STATE; established boundary review_interval >= interval '24 hours'
query_behavior.empty_result_behavior: no sections (or unknown essay_id) -> empty Dataset rows: [], not an error
query_behavior.zero_fill_behavior: n/a - every section appears exactly once; a section with no oral-state row reports guided_passed=false, unguided_passed=false, scores null, state 'grey'
query_behavior.row_shape: section_id, essay_id, heading, anchor_slug, order_index (string/number); state ('grey'|'yellow'|'green'|'blue'); next_step ('guided_oral'|'flashcards_established'|'unguided_oral'|null); guided_passed, unguided_passed (boolean); guided_pass_source ('exam'|'grandfathered'|null); guided_latest_score, unguided_latest_score (number|null, 0-6); guided_passed_at, unguided_passed_at (date|null); cards_total, cards_established (number); is_locked (boolean, true iff not guided_passed)

exposed_surfaces.name: GET /api/essaycards/essays
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Essay overview rows. Keeps category-level counts; replaces the Sprint12 learning-progress fields with the derived essay traffic light.

query_behavior.ordering: unchanged - category asc nulls last, sort_index asc, created_at asc
query_behavior.time_basis: Postgres now() for open_count only; essay_state is clock-independent
query_behavior.boundary_construction: contracts.invariants ESSAY STATE; learned boundary review_interval >= interval '30 days'
query_behavior.zero_fill_behavior: counts default 0, essay_state 'grey' for an essay with no oral state; never null for the new count/boolean fields
query_behavior.row_shape: UNCHANGED: id, title, slug, category, sort_index, status, progress_total, progress_established, created_at, updated_at. CHANGED: open_count (now excludes locked and needs_revalidation cards). REMOVED: cards_seen_count, cards_future_safe_count, milestone_all_cards_seen, milestone_all_cards_future_safe, milestone_guided_passed, milestone_unguided_passed, guided_passed_at, unguided_passed_at, learning_level. NEW: essay_state ('grey'|'yellow'|'green'|'blue'|'violet'); essay_next_step ('guided_essay_oral'|'cards_learned'|'section_unguided_orals'|'unguided_essay_oral'|null); essay_guided_passed, essay_unguided_passed (boolean); essay_guided_latest_score, essay_unguided_latest_score (number|null); essay_guided_passed_at, essay_unguided_passed_at (date|null); cards_learned_count, sections_total, sections_unguided_passed_count, revalidation_pending_count (number)

internal_flow.name: schema_additions
internal_flow.description: 10_schema.sql: section_examinations.passed (one-time backfill), essay_examinations, essay_oral_state, section_oral_state (+ one-time grandfathering backfill guarded by the table's own absence), flashcard_review_state.needs_revalidation, revalidation_events. Folded into schema.sql after the Sprint13 block, inside schema.sql's single existing begin/commit (10_schema.sql carries no transaction statements of its own).

internal_flow.name: pass_rule_module
internal_flow.description: backend/oral_state.py defines SCORE_MAX=6, PASS_THRESHOLD_PERCENT=70 and is_passing_score(score) (integer arithmetic: score*100 >= PASS_THRESHOLD_PERCENT*SCORE_MAX). Every verdict - import validation echo, package scoring echo, stored passed - flows from this one function. Sprint12's PASS_SCORE_THRESHOLD and its SQL literal '< 3' are deleted with the nine old progress fields.

internal_flow.name: examination_package_scope
internal_flow.description: build_export_package gains scope/section_id. scope=section restricts sections to the one section (404 if it is not in the essay). scope=essay keeps every section and, for exam_type=guided, adds last_essay_examination from essay_examinations. exam_type=unguided still emits null calibration everywhere. The scoring echo is built from backend.oral_state constants. The router validates the parameter combination manually (VALIDATION_ERROR) before touching the DB.

internal_flow.name: import_validation
internal_flow.description: validate_import_body gains per-result scope (required, 'section'|'essay'). scope=section: unchanged requirements (section_anchor_slug, section_version, nugget_versions). scope=essay: section_anchor_slug must be absent/null; section_version and nugget_versions are accepted and IGNORED (examiners may echo them; they are not stored for essay scope); essay_slug, examined_at, question, answer_transcript, score, exam_type, feedback validated identically to section results. Each validated result gains passed = is_passing_score(score).
outputs: validated result dicts with scope and passed

internal_flow.name: import_apply_attempts
internal_flow.description: import_results resolves every (essay_slug[, section_anchor_slug]) first (NOT_FOUND rejects the whole batch), then, in array order inside the caller's transaction: INSERT the attempt (section_examinations incl. passed, or essay_examinations), then call apply_section_attempt / apply_essay_attempt. Each returns an effects list. The response record gains per result: scope, passed, score_percent (one decimal), effects; and top-level revalidation: {essay_id, cards_flagged} entries for every cascade that fired.

internal_flow.name: apply_state_transitions
internal_flow.description: apply_section_attempt(cur, section_id, exam_type, score, passed, examined_at): upsert section_oral_state (create row on first attempt); always set the matching *_latest_score; guided + passed -> guided_passed=true, guided_pass_source='exam', guided_passed_at=examined_at; unguided + passed -> unguided_passed=true, unguided_passed_at=examined_at, unguided_invalidated_at=null; failures change only latest_score. Returns effects like 'section_guided_unlocked' (only when guided_passed flips false->true) / 'section_unguided_passed'. apply_essay_attempt mirrors this on essay_oral_state; an unguided essay failure while unguided_passed was true runs the FAILURE CASCADE (invariants) and returns effect 'essay_unguided_failed_cascade' with cards_flagged. The prior-state read and the cascade use insert-if-absent (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) of the essay_oral_state row followed by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on it, so two concurrent failing imports cascade once.

internal_flow.name: derived_progress_sql
internal_flow.description: backend/progress.py is the single home of the Established/Learned thresholds and of every progress derivation. section_progress_sql() returns the per-section state query (LEFT JOIN section_oral_state, aggregate over flashcards x flashcard_review_state). essay_progress_lateral_sql() is the LATERAL fragment (essay alias e) computing essay_state and its supporting counts, itself reusing the section query for 'every section unguided'. CARD_STATE_SQL is the per-card CASE expression. UNLOCKED_SECTION_SQL is the reusable predicate fragment (EXISTS section_oral_state ... guided_passed) used by /due, /stats, open_count and card_state. next_step is the first unmet rung in the ladder (section: guided_oral -> flashcards_established -> unguided_oral; essay: guided_essay_oral -> cards_learned -> section_unguided_orals -> unguided_essay_oral), null only at the top rung of the respective ladder: section next_step is null when the section state is blue; essay_next_step is null when the essay state is violet (an essay at Blue reports unguided_essay_oral).

internal_flow.name: essays_endpoints_field_swap
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/essays.py: _learning_progress_subquery_sql, its nine fields, learning_level, PASS_SCORE_THRESHOLD and the guided/unguided_latest CTEs are REMOVED; ESSAY_OVERVIEW_SCHEMA loses the nine ColumnSchema entries and gains the new essay fields; _OVERVIEW_QUERY and get_essay use progress.essay_progress_lateral_sql(); open_count adds the unlocked/not-flagged predicates; _row_to_dict date-key list updated. list_essay_questions joins review state + unlock predicate to emit is_locked, card_state, needs_revalidation.

internal_flow.name: progress_sections_endpoint
internal_flow.description: backend/routers/progress.py::list_section_progress runs section_progress_sql(), optionally filtered by essay_id, ordered per query_behavior, returned as a flat Dataset.

internal_flow.name: queue_eligibility_filters
internal_flow.description: flashcards.py::list_due_flashcards appends the UNLOCKED_SECTION_SQL predicate and frs.needs_revalidation = false to its conditions list; flashcard_queue_stats appends only the unlock predicate. No ORDER BY, scope-validation or select-list change.

internal_flow.name: revalidation_queue_endpoint
internal_flow.description: flashcards.py::list_revalidation_cards (GET /flashcards/revalidation, declared before the /{flashcard_id}/... routes) selects the DUE_SCHEMA row shape for every flagged card (optionally one essay) in the deterministic order from query_behavior and returns _due_dataset(rows).

internal_flow.name: review_endpoint_revalidation_branch
internal_flow.description: review_flashcard, after loading the review-state row (now also selecting needs_revalidation) and the section unlock state: (a) locked -> VALIDATION_ERROR. (b) needs_revalidation false -> existing path byte-for-byte unchanged, response revalidation_outcome null. (c) needs_revalidation true and is_revalidation_correct(grade) -> clear flag, record_revalidation_event(outcome 'preserved'), commit; response echoes the card's EXISTING last_reviewed_at/next_due_at, revalidation_outcome 'preserved'. (d) needs_revalidation true and not correct -> run the existing FSRS path, clear flag in the same UPDATE/transaction, record_revalidation_event(outcome 'failed'); response as normal plus revalidation_outcome 'failed'. All branches in one transaction.

internal_flow.name: overview_ui
internal_flow.description: EssayListView: each essay row drops StatusPill, the 'Progress: x / y . Open: z' line, the sort-index-adjacent LearningLevelBadge; it renders EssayProgressDot (large) + SectionProgressDots (small, one per section in order) built from GET /essays + GET /progress/sections (two parallel fetches; sections grouped client-side by essay_id). Dot tooltip/tap reveals section/essay title, current state name, next requirement (from next_step). A legend disclosure (ProgressLegend) lists both ladders. Category headings and their established/open/Study controls are untouched. An essay with revalidation_pending_count > 0 shows a 'Revalidate (N)' control navigating to /essaycards/review?revalidate=1&essay_id=<id>. Dots must carry an accessible text label (state name), never color alone.

internal_flow.name: reader_and_oral_launch_ui

internal_flow.name: revalidation_session_ui
internal_flow.description: ReviewSessionView reads revalidate=1: dueUrl() targets /flashcards/revalidation (with essay_id), scopeLabel is 'Revalidation', the forecast ReviewStatsPanel and the today-metrics row are not rendered, a 'N remaining' count (queue.length) is shown, and grading sends the unchanged {grade} body. Because answered cards leave the queue (flag cleared), refetch-on-grade empties it; the completion screen reads 'Revalidation complete' and links back to the overview. The revalidation grade control is exactly TWO buttons, 'Correct' and 'Incorrect' (the standard four again/hard/good/easy buttons are NOT shown in revalidation mode, so there is no 'Hard' button and no ambiguous 'Hard' outcome). Mapping: 'Correct' sends {grade: 'good'} = correct (outcome 'preserved', no FSRS change); 'Incorrect' sends {grade: 'again'} = incorrect (outcome 'failed', normal FSRS again path). Only these two values from VALID_GRADES are sent by the UI; the server still treats hard/easy as correct for stale or non-UI clients (REVALIDATION CARD HANDLING is unchanged).

risks.risk: Migration lock-out: the new unlock rule would lock every existing card.
risks.impact: Mitigated by the one-time grandfathering backfill (any section with a reviewed card or a guided exam >= 3 becomes guided_passed with source 'grandfathered'). A section that has neither (never started) correctly starts locked. If the backfill logic is wrong, a user's whole queue disappears - hence the dedicated migration test.

risks.risk: The 70% rule on a 0-6 scale makes the pass bar 5/6, stricter than the Sprint12 bar of 3/6; historical attempts scoring 3-4 stop counting as passes.
risks.impact: Previously 'passed' orals no longer advance new progression (grandfathering protects existing unlocks only). See open_questions for the alternative of changing the examiner scale.

risks.risk: Essay Green requires every card of the essay to be Learned, and a card in a locked section can never be reviewed.
risks.impact: An essay can only reach Green after every section has passed its guided oral; this is a consequence of the draft, intended, but may surprise.

risks.risk: State is applied in import order, not examined_at order.
risks.impact: Importing an old result after a newer one can flip state against chronological truth. Accepted and documented; same append-only trust model as Sprint12.

risks.risk: Removing the nine Sprint12 fields from GET /essays and GET /essays/{id} is a breaking Dataset change.
risks.impact: Only the EssayCards frontend consumes them (verified by grep: ShellEntry.tsx, tests); it is reworked in the same sprint (R-CON-BP-09). Any stale cached frontend bundle would render NaN/undefined levels until redeployed.

risks.risk: Excluding flagged cards from /due while they await revalidation can leave a user with an empty normal queue and pending revalidation.
risks.impact: Intentional; mitigated by surfacing the Revalidate (N) control on the overview, reader and import result.

open_questions.question: Pass threshold on the existing 0-6 integer scale: 70% means score >= 5 (4/6 = 66.7% fails), versus Sprint12's >= 3. Is that intended, or should examiners score on a 0-100 scale (which would need a score column/constraint change and a prompt change)? This design implements 70% of 6 and parameterizes only the constant.

Draft section 13 says 'when an unguided full-essay oral is failed, initiate Revalidation' while section 12 scopes the consequences to an essay currently at Violet. This design runs the cascade and revalidation only when essay unguided_passed was true at the time of the failing attempt; a first-ever failing unguided essay oral is history-only. Confirm.
Draft says revalidation covers 'all active flashcards'. This design flags only cards that have been reviewed at least once (a never-reviewed card has no memory state to validate). Confirm.

Grandfathering of existing sections (any reviewed card or guided exam >= 3 -> guided_passed, source 'grandfathered'). Confirm this one-time rule, or specify that existing sections should start locked.

Open count wording: 'category-level flashcard statistics unchanged' vs open_count's definition 'what a focus session surfaces'. This design keeps progress_total/progress_established unchanged but makes open_count exclude locked and revalidation-pending cards. Confirm, or accept the overstated open count (and Study buttons that open an empty session) for fully locked essays.
Should a failed unguided SECTION oral revoke that section's Blue (draft only specifies the essay-level failure cascade)? Design: no.
Oral-exam buttons remain disabled unless essay.status === 'complete', although the draft says planned/complete is 'no longer needed' on the card. Keep that gating?
